chunks: Hamza ibn Muhammad al-Alawi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Hasani narrated to me. He said: Abu Husayn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Wadi'i the judge narrated to me. He said: Ahmad ibn Subayh narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Amr ibn Thabit, from al-Sadiq Jafar ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both). He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin (peace be upon him) said to me:
regarding the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic, 'Forgive with gracious forgiveness' [15:85].

key_terms.الصفح الجميل: Gracious forgiveness — the Quranic term for forgiving without holding a grudge or rebuking the wrongdoer
key_terms.العتاب: Blame, reproach — the act of reminding or rebuking someone for their fault
key_terms.العفو: Pardon, forgiveness — the act of releasing another from blame or obligation

ai.seo_question: What does 'forgive with gracious forgiveness' mean according to Imam Zayn al-Abidin?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS), the fourth Imam, explains the Quranic injunction in Surah al-Hijr (15:85) to 'forgive with gracious forgiveness.' The Imam defines this as forgiveness that carries no accompanying reproach or blame toward the one being forgiven. This teaching, transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq and his father Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon them), clarifies that true forgiveness in Islam is complete and dignified — it does not involve reminding the offender of their wrongdoing.
